# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 14 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_014_page_001.jpg

---

1 Again, one who is about to sail and intends to pass through savage waves calls upon wood more fragile than the vessel bearing him.

2 For that vessel desire for gain devised, and wisdom was the craftsman who fashioned it;

3 but it is your providence, O Father, that steers it, because you have given a path even in the sea, and a safe way through the waves,

4 demonstrating that you are able to save from every danger, so that even someone without experience may put to sea.

5 Yet it is your will that the works of your wisdom should not be without effect; therefore people entrust their lives to the very smallest piece of wood, and passing through the surge upon a raft, reach safety.

6 For even in the beginning, when arrogant giants were perishing, the hope of the world, taking refuge on a raft, guided by your hand, left to the age a seed of generations to come.

7 For blessed is wood through which righteousness is wrought.

8 But the idol made by hands is accursed — both it and the one who made it: he, because he made it; it, because, though perishable, it was named a god.

9 For equally hateful to God are the ungodly and his ungodliness,

10 and both the deed and the one who did it will be punished.

11 For this reason, upon the idols of the nations too there will be a visitation, because in the creation of God they became an abomination, a stumbling block to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the foolish.

12 For the devising of idols was the beginning of fornication, and the invention of them the corruption of life.

13 For neither did they exist from the beginning, nor will they endure forever.

14 For through the empty vanity of men they entered the world, and therefore their rapid end has been devised.

15 For a father, consumed with grief over a child taken untimely, made an image of the one so quickly taken away, and now honored as a god what was once a dead human being, and handed on to those beneath him secret rites and ceremonies.

16 Then in the course of time the ungodly custom was strengthened and observed as law, and graven images were worshipped at the command of monarchs.

17 And when people could not honor them in their presence because they lived at a distance, they pictured the distant appearance and made a visible likeness of the king they honored, so that through their zeal they might flatter the absent one as though present.

18 But the ambition of the craftsman drove even those who did not know the king to intensify their worship,

19 for he, wishing to please his patron, pressed his art to produce a finer likeness,

20 and the crowd, attracted by the beauty of his work, came to regard as an object of devotion the one whom shortly before they had honored as a man.

21 And this became a hidden trap for life, because people, enslaved either to misfortune or to tyranny, assigned to stones and sticks the Name that cannot be shared.

22 Then it was not enough for them to go astray in their knowledge of God; but while living in a great war of ignorance, they call such great evils peace.

23 For either performing child-slaughter in their rites, or celebrating hidden mysteries, or holding frenzied revels with outlandish ceremonies,

24 they no longer guard either the purity of life or the sanctity of marriage; but one either slays another by treachery, or injures him by adultery.

25 And over all there reigns a confusion of blood and murder, theft and fraud, corruption, treachery, riot, perjury,

26 the disquieting of good men, ingratitude for kindnesses, pollution of souls, perversion of sex, disorder in marriage, adultery, and debauchery.

27 For the worship of the unspeakable idols is the beginning and cause and end of all evil.

28 For they either make merry with exultation, or prophesy lies, or live wickedly, or readily perjure themselves.

29 For since they put their trust in lifeless idols, when they swear falsely they expect to suffer no harm.

30 But just retribution will pursue them on two counts: because they thought perversely about God in giving themselves to idols, and because they swore unrighteously in deceit, despising holiness.

31 For it is not the power of those by whom oaths are sworn, but the just penalty of sinners, that always pursues the transgression of the unrighteous.
